summary: Long-tail request histogram from single tenant caused autoscaler bias and gradual GPU credit depletion
description: Issue summary: Over the 2026-03-05 midday window a dedicated customer (ParcelAI) experienced a slow, progressive degradation of dedicated throughput. P50 remained stable but p95/p99 drifted up and overall token throughput dropped ~20% over 3 hours. Impact: customer-facing latency increases and eventual fallback to lower-capacity model variants for some routes. Environment: prod us-east-1 on dedicated pool DED-AZ3. Observed behavior: autoscaler stopped scaling up after initial minor increases and allocator started returning fewer GPU attach tokens for ParcelAI; autoscaler metrics show strong skew in request duration histogram (very long tail from certain sessions) causing smoothing logic to undercount short bursts and bias capacity decisioning. Steps to reproduce: 1) Run sustained mix of small short-streams and intermittent very long, high-context requests from a single tenant; 2) Observe autoscaler histogram bins shifting and allocator credit consumption; 3) See gradual p99 rise and eventual attach backoff. Additional notes: customer uses a custom SDK that keeps a pool of long-lived gRPC connections and issues occasional very long-context generation requests (many thousands of tokens) mixed with bursty short requests. This mixed pattern appears to inflate the tail without producing steady median load, confusing the autoscaler smoothing window.
steps_to_reproduce: Start a dedicated tenant pool in us-east-1
Open 200 long-lived gRPC connections from one client
Send intermittent 10k token generation requests on 1% of connections and short 1-3 token requests on the rest
Observe autoscaler histogram and allocator attach counts over 2-4 hours

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: noisy-neighbor small-stream fanout (ruled out) — aggregate traffic pattern shows skew from a single tenant rather than many tenants.
Telemetry: tenant-level request-duration histogram has heavy right tail; autoscaler smoothing uses median-weighted window that currently underweights low-throughput long-tail signals.
Allocator: GPU attach credits were being consumed by a small number of very long jobs; those jobs held slots for extended time, preventing batched short requests from using GPUs efficiently.
KV-cache: Prefetch growth tracked with long requests; cache pins increased memory pressure on assigned GPUs, contributing to slower per-token throughput for mixed workloads.
comments: 2026-03-05 12:30 - Support (Aisha): Notified ParcelAI CS rep and asked for SDK usage patterns and sample client traces.

2026-03-05 13:05 - ParcelAI (K. Nguyen): Confirmed they use an internally modified SDK that keeps ~150 persistent gRPC streams and occasionally sends multi-thousand token summaries during business-hours processing.

2026-03-05 14:20 - SRE (Diego): Applied temporary tenant throttling rule to limit concurrent long-context requests to 4 while keeping short stream concurrency unchanged. Observed immediate drop in p99 and upward recovery of attach counts.
2026-03-07 09:12 - Eng (Mei Chen): Started work on autoscaler histogram smoothing change to incorporate tail-decay factor and a per-tenant long-job cap in allocator. PR opened for design review.
root_cause: Autoscaler decisioning was biased by a heavy-tailed per-tenant request-duration distribution. The smoothing algorithm prioritized stable medians and under-reacted to sporadic, long-running requests that consumed GPU slots for extended periods. Combined with aggressive kv-cache prefetch for long contexts, the tenant effectively hoarded GPU attachment time resulting in gradual GPU credit depletion for the dedicated pool.
workaround: Applied a temporary server-side concurrency cap for long-context requests from ParcelAI and set a tenant-level throttling policy to limit prefetch TTL. This freed GPU slots for short requests and returned p99 latency to baseline within ~20 minutes.
resolution: Workaround applied; longer-term autoscaler/allocator changes in progress
resolution_notes: Temporary throttles deployed 2026-03-05 14:20 UTC: limited concurrent long-context jobs per tenant to 4.
Short-term patch to allocator: mark slots held by long-lived requests as low-parallelism candidates to allow opportunistic short-request scheduling (rolled to staging 2026-03-06).
Planned change: autoscaler histogram smoothing to include tail-decay factor and per-tenant heavy-job quota; target release 2026-03-20.
Customer action: ParcelAI agreed to ship an SDK update that exposes long-job hints so server can tag requests; customer ETA for SDK release 2026-03-18.
